name: Assurex
description: Assurex is a precision dopamine-norepinephrine modulator engineered to produce sustained, realistic confidence without the manic edge of stimulants or the social disinhibition of alcohol. It amplifies self-efficacy signals in the prefrontal cortex while reducing the threat-appraisal response, resulting in a calm, grounded certainty. It is heavily marketed for high-stakes professional situations: job interviews, corporate presentations, contract negotiations, and performance reviews.
effects: Elevated sense of personal competence and self-efficacy
Reduced threat-appraisal — confrontations feel manageable rather than threatening
Improved eye contact and body language regulation via BCI feedback
Suppression of imposter syndrome and self-doubt loops
Mild analgesic effect — physical discomfort doesn't register as distressing
side_effects: Confidence that outstrips actual competence — users may commit to things they cannot deliver
Post-dose confidence crash — users feel acutely inadequate when drug clears
Dependency: users become unable to face high-stakes situations without it
Blunted social calibration — users may be perceived as arrogant or dismissive
At high doses: reckless decision-making indistinguishable from mania
cultural_context: Assurex is the open secret of GLMZ's corporate tier. Tier 3-4 professionals use it so routinely for interviews and presentations that HR departments have started specifying 'Assurex-free assessment environments' — which no one enforces. On the street, it's called 'the Edge' and used before confrontations, debt negotiations, and Shelf turf disputes. Helix markets it with the slogan 'You, optimized' — which its critics say is precisely the problem. There's an emerging subculture of Assurex dependency support groups in Tier 2, full of people who can no longer remember how to walk into a room without it.
story_hooks: A fixer took Assurex before a negotiation, committed to terms she cannot possibly fulfill, and now needs to either find a way to deliver or convince the other party to renegotiate — with someone who also took Assurex before the meeting.

A Tier 4 executive's teenage child has been stealing Assurex to get through school presentations. The dependency is progressing fast and the kid is starting to use it for situations that don't require it — like talking to friends.

Someone has been slipping Assurex into a target's food before interrogations — not to make them talk, but to make them commit to false confessions with absolute conviction. The people processing those confessions have no idea.
